title: King Teen Patti — Game Server
description: System, Go runtime, WebSockets, game, latency, PostgreSQL and nginx for the King Teen Patti server (Requirements 35–36).

links.title: Runbook (MONITORING.md)
links.tooltip: What each panel means and what to do when it goes red

list.name: datname
list.label: PostgreSQL database
list.description: The database the game server uses; pg_stat_database_* and pg_locks_count are filtered to it.

panels.title: CPU %
panels.description: Share of all cores busy over the last 5 minutes (node_exporter).

panels.title: RAM usage
panels.description: Memory not available to new allocations (MemTotal − MemAvailable); page cache counts as available.

panels.title: Swap usage
panels.description: Any sustained swap use on a game host means the game server's or PostgreSQL's working set no longer fits in RAM. Reads 0 when the machine has no swap.

panels.title: Disk usage (root fs)
panels.description: Used share of the root filesystem. PostgreSQL (chip_ledger grows on every move) and Prometheus both live here unless moved.

panels.title: CPU %
panels.description: Host CPU as a fraction of all cores. iowait rising with PostgreSQL commits means the disk, not the CPU, is the limit.

panels.title: RAM usage
panels.description: Used = MemTotal − MemAvailable. Cache and buffers are reclaimable and not counted as used; swap used should stay at zero.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: Runnable + uninterruptible tasks. Sustained load above the dashed core count means work is queueing.

panels.title: Network RX
panels.description: Bits per second received on physical interfaces (loopback, docker and veth excluded).

panels.title: Network TX
panels.description: Bits per second sent. Every table state change is one message per seated viewer; this scales with players × hands.

panels.title: Open file descriptors
panels.description: One descriptor per websocket in the game server (plus the pg pool and logs) and two per proxied websocket in nginx. The dashed line is the game server process's RLIMIT_NOFILE — raise it with the systemd drop-in in ops/monitoring/nginx/systemd/.

panels.title: TCP connections
panels.description: Established TCP connections on the host ≈ 2 × websockets (client→nginx and nginx→game server) + PostgreSQL + scrapes.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Seconds since the game server process started (game_server_process_uptime_seconds). A reset here with no deploy is a crash — check the restart annotation and journalctl -u gameplay.

panels.title: Go version
panels.description: Runtime version reported by the process (game_server_go_info). The Go binary reports the same string as /health process.node.

panels.title: Started at
panels.description: Wall-clock time the process started (game_server_process_start_time_seconds).

panels.title: RSS memory
panels.description: Resident set size of the game server process — what the OS actually holds in RAM for it.

panels.title: Heap in use
panels.description: Go heap spans in use (game_server_go_memstats_heap_inuse_bytes): live objects plus the unused part of the spans they sit in. Saw-tooths with the GC; a rising floor is a leak.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Live goroutines (game_server_go_goroutines). One per table actor, a few per websocket, plus timers. Roughly 3 × sockets + tables at rest; the GameServerGoroutinesHigh alert fires above 50,000.

panels.title: RSS memory
panels.description: Resident set size and what the Go runtime has asked the OS for: total (sys), the heap arena and goroutine stacks. RSS well above sys means memory outside the runtime (kernel socket buffers, the binary itself).

panels.title: Heap
panels.description: alloc = bytes in live objects right now; in use = spans holding them; live = what survived the last GC (the real working set); goal = heap size that triggers the next GC (GOGC, default 100 → about 2 × live). A rising 'live' with a flat player count is a leak.

panels.title: Goroutines & threads
panels.description: Total goroutines, the ones runnable but not yet scheduled (a growing runnable count means the CPUs are saturated) and OS threads. Red line: the GameServerGoroutinesHigh alert (50,000 for 5 min) — a leak of per-socket or per-table goroutines.

panels.title: Open file descriptors
panels.description: Descriptors held by the game server process: one per websocket, the pg pool, the listener, logs. Dashed line: RLIMIT_NOFILE (LimitNOFILE=65536 in gameplay.service). The GameServerFileDescriptorsHigh alert fires at 80 %.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU seconds per second used by the process. Unlike Node, the Go server uses every core (GOMAXPROCS = all cores by default); the dashed line is that ceiling. Compare with the host CPU % in the System row.

panels.title: Scheduler latency
panels.description: How long runnable goroutines wait before they get a CPU (game_server_go_sched_latencies_seconds) — the Go equivalent of Node's event-loop lag: a move's ack, a broadcast, a turn timer all queue behind it. Red line: the GameServerSchedulerLatencyHigh alert (p99 > 100 ms for 5 min). Bucket edges are coarse (~1 ms, ~10 ms, ~117 ms), so values are interpolated within a bucket.

panels.title: GC pauses
panels.description: Stop-the-world pause lengths. p99 from the runtime histogram over 5 min (game_server_go_sched_pauses_total_gc_seconds); median and max from the game_server_go_gc_duration_seconds summary (last 256 cycles). Go pauses are sub-millisecond; anything above 10 ms is worth a look at heap size and allocation rate.

panels.title: GC activity
panels.description: Left axis: share of wall time spent in stop-the-world GC pauses (rate of game_server_go_gc_duration_seconds_sum). Right axis: GC cycles per second. Many cycles with a small heap = a high allocation rate; tune with GOGC or GOMEMLIMIT in the unit's Environment= if it ever matters.

panels.title: Process network I/O
panels.description: Bytes per second the game server process itself receives and transmits (game_server_process_network_*_bytes_total): websocket frames to and from nginx plus PostgreSQL traffic. Compare with the host's Network RX/TX in the System row.

panels.title: Heap objects & allocation rate
panels.description: Left axis: live heap objects (game_server_go_memstats_heap_objects) — a leak detector when players are flat. Right axis: allocations per second (rate of game_server_go_memstats_mallocs_total), which drives GC frequency.

panels.title: Connected sockets
panels.description: Socket.IO connections open now. Thresholds mirror the king_teenpatti:socket_limit recording rule (12,000).

panels.title: Peak connected sockets
panels.description: Highest simultaneous connection count since the process started. Resets on restart.

panels.title: Connections/sec
panels.description: New Socket.IO connections accepted per second over the last minute.

panels.title: Messages/sec
panels.description: Client → server messages of every event type.

panels.title: Connected sockets
panels.description: Connected vs seated: the gap is players in the lobby or on the login screen.

panels.title: Connections/sec
panels.description: session replaced = the same account signed in from a second device and the first socket was closed.

panels.title: Disconnections/sec (by reason)
panels.description: Socket.IO disconnect reasons. "transport close" / "ping timeout" are network drops (the seat is held for RECONNECT_GRACE_MS); "client namespace disconnect" is the app closing cleanly; "server namespace disconnect" is a kick or session replacement.

panels.title: Reconnects/sec
panels.description: Players who came back while their seat was still held, or who were offered their previous table back on sign-in (session:ready.resume).

panels.title: Messages/sec (by event, top 10)
panels.description: Inbound events. game:action dominates during play; ping:rtt is the client's latency probe.

panels.title: Emits/sec (by event, top 10)
panels.description: Outbound events; a room broadcast counts once, a per-viewer room:state counts once per viewer.

panels.title: Errors/sec (by code)
panels.description: Requests refused on the socket. rate_limited and not_your_turn are client behaviour; persist_failed or internal_error is ours.

panels.title: Players online
panels.description: Players seated at a table right now (not lobby visitors — see WebSockets → Connected sockets for those).

panels.title: Active games
panels.description: Tables with a hand in progress.

panels.title: Waiting games
panels.description: Tables between hands or waiting for a second player.

panels.title: Open tables
panels.description: Tables in memory across every category and stake (= active + waiting games).

panels.title: Players & games
panels.description: Seated players against the number of tables with and without a hand running. At full tables players ≈ 5 × active games.

panels.title: Tables by category / stake
panels.description: Open tables per lobby entry (seen 200, blind 200, blind 5000; private tables appear under their category with the private boot).

panels.title: Games started/sec
panels.description: Hands dealt per second, by table category. The 2026-09-08 load test ran ~23 hands/s at 1,500 players.

panels.title: Games completed/sec (by reason)
panels.description: last_standing = everyone else packed; show = a paid show; forced_showdown = round cap; pot_limit = table max pot reached.

panels.title: Games abandoned/sec
panels.description: Hands that ended because every player left (all_left) or the table was destroyed mid-hand. Should be near zero; a step up alongside disconnections is a network incident.

panels.title: Moves/sec (by action)
panels.description: Accepted actions: see, chaal, raise, pack, show, sideshow. Each chaal/raise/show is one ledger transaction.

panels.title: Invalid moves/sec (by code)
panels.description: Refused actions. not_your_turn / invalid_bet at a low rate are clients racing the clock; duplicate_action is the idempotency guard doing its job; a spike of insufficient_chips means the ladder and the clients disagree.

panels.title: Turn timeouts & kicks/sec
panels.description: A turn that ran out the 25 s clock is auto-packed; three in a row is a kick (idle). unfunded = below the boot between hands.

panels.title: Chat messages/sec & chips paid out/sec
panels.description: Right axis: chips credited to winners per second — the throughput of the settle transaction.

panels.title: Move P50
panels.description: Median time to process a move over the last 5 minutes (all actions).

panels.title: Move P90
panels.description: 90th percentile move processing time over the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Move P95
panels.description: 95th percentile move processing time over the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Move P99
panels.description: 99th percentile move processing time over the last 5 minutes. The GameServerMoveLatencyHigh alert fires above 500 ms.

panels.title: Move processing latency
panels.description: Validate → ledger transaction → table update, all actions. Quantiles are interpolated within the bucket boundaries (1 ms … 1 s), so a value above 1 s is a lower bound.

panels.title: Move P95 by action
panels.description: see and pack touch no chips and should be sub-millisecond; chaal/raise/show include a database round trip.

panels.title: Game creation latency
panels.description: Time to open a new table (quick-join that found no room, or room:create).

panels.title: Game join latency
panels.description: From the join request to the player seated and sent the table snapshot, all entry routes.

panels.title: Game join P95 by route
panels.description: quickJoin (lobby), joinCode (private / resume offer), switch (room:switch), create.

panels.title: State update latency
panels.description: Serialising the table once per viewer (redaction) and emitting to all of them. Runs on the event loop — if this grows, event-loop lag follows.

panels.title: DB transaction P95 by op
panels.description: The ledger transactions that move chips: bet (one wallet row lock), boot (every player's wallet, locked in id order), settle (pot to winner). Compare with PostgreSQL → Transactions/sec.

panels.title: Hand start & settlement P95
panels.description: Collecting the boot and dealing (one transaction) and paying the winner. Settlement failures retry in the background and show under DB transaction errors.

panels.title: DB transaction errors/sec
panels.description: Rolled-back ledger transactions. duplicate_action = a retried request refused by the UNIQUE action_id (benign). stale_state = two processes think they own one table. Anything else is a database problem.

panels.title: PostgreSQL
panels.description: postgres_exporter can reach the database.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Backends connected to $datname (pg_stat_database_numbackends).

panels.title: Active connections
panels.description: Backends executing a query right now.

panels.title: Idle connections
panels.description: idle, idle in transaction and idle in transaction (aborted). The game server's pool keeps up to PG_POOL_MAX idle.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: blks_hit / (blks_hit + blks_read) over 5 minutes. Below 0.9 the working set no longer fits shared_buffers.

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: On-disk size of $datname (pg_database_size_bytes).

panels.title: Connections by state
panels.description: All backends on $datname by state, against the server-wide max_connections.

panels.title: Queries/sec (proxy)
panels.description: PostgreSQL keeps no per-database statement counter, so this shows rows returned/fetched per second as a proxy for query volume. For true queries/sec: add pg_stat_statements to shared_preload_libraries, CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements in gameplay, start postgres_exporter with --collector.stat_statements, then plot sum(rate(pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="gameplay"}[1m])).

panels.title: Transactions/sec
panels.description: Commits ≈ moves/s + hands/s × 2 (boot + settle) + logins. Rollbacks that are not duplicate_action refusals need a look at the server log.

panels.title: Rows/sec
panels.description: Every bet inserts one chip_ledger row and updates users + pots + game_states. Deletes should be ~0: chip_ledger is append-only by trigger.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of block reads served from shared_buffers (5-minute window). The PostgresCacheHitRatioLow alert fires below the red line while reads are happening.

panels.title: Locks (by mode)
panels.description: Locks held on $datname. rowexclusivelock spikes are the ledger's SELECT … FOR UPDATE on wallets; accessexclusivelock means DDL or VACUUM FULL.

panels.title: Deadlocks
panels.description: Deadlocks detected in the last 5 minutes. The ledger locks wallets in ascending user id order precisely so this stays at zero.

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: Grows with chip_ledger (one row per chip movement, never deleted) and hands.

panels.title: App-side pg pool
panels.description: The game server's own pg Pool (PG_POOL_MAX, default 10). Waiting requests > 0 means every connection is busy and moves are queueing — the GameServerDbPoolSaturated alert.

panels.title: nginx
panels.description: nginx-prometheus-exporter can read stub_status.

panels.title: Active connections
panels.description: Client connections open, including idle keep-alive and every websocket. Does not include the upstream leg — nginx uses two descriptors per proxied websocket.

panels.title: Reading
panels.description: Connections whose request headers are being read.

panels.title: Writing
panels.description: Connections being written to. Every open websocket sits here.

panels.title: Waiting
panels.description: Idle keep-alive connections waiting for the next request.

panels.title: Requests/sec
panels.description: HTTP requests nginx served per second, including Socket.IO handshakes and polling.

panels.title: Connection states
panels.description: stub_status counters. The red line is 80% of worker_processes × worker_connections from nginx.conf.example (4 × 16384); update it with the config.

panels.title: Requests/sec
panels.description: nginx counts every HTTP request including Socket.IO handshakes and polling; the game server counts only REST responses (the websocket upgrade is not counted).

panels.title: Accepted vs handled/sec
panels.description: accepted − handled > 0 is nginx running out of worker_connections — the failure that capped the 2026-09-08 load test at ~1,500 players with HTTP 500 on every new handshake. Fires the NginxDroppingConnections alert.

panels.title: 5xx errors/sec
panels.description: Server errors per second, from the application's own counter (game_http_requests_total). nginx-prometheus-exporter reads stub_status, which has NO per-status counters, so errors nginx generates itself — 502 with the game server down, 500 "worker_connections are not enough", 504 upstream timeouts — are not in this panel. To see those: (a) build nginx with the VTS module (github.com/vozlt/nginx-module-vts), add `vhost_traffic_status_zone;` in http{} and a `location /status { vhost_traffic_status_display; vhost_traffic_status_display_format prometheus; }`, scrape it and plot sum(rate(nginx_vts_server_requests_total{code="5xx"}[1m])); or (b) run prometheus-nginxlog-exporter (github.com/martin-helmich/prometheus-nginxlog-exporter) on /var/log/nginx/king-teenpatti.access.log and plot sum(rate(nginx_http_response_count_total{status=~"5.."}[1m])). MONITORING.md → Nginx has the steps.

panels.title: Game server HTTP responses/sec by status class
panels.description: 2xx / 4xx / 5xx share of REST responses. 4xx is mostly 401 from expired tokens and 409 from renaming while seated.

panels.title: Game server HTTP P95 by route
panels.description: REST latency by route pattern (never a raw URL). /api/auth/login includes the provider round-trip.

panels.title: Redis up
panels.description: 1 when redis_exporter can reach the live-state store. The game server keeps playing without it; a restart would then lose tables in progress.

panels.title: Live keys
panels.description: Keys in the store: table snapshots, seats, presence, resume offers and the matchmaking index.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Redis resident memory against its 512 MB cap.

panels.title: Tables restored (last start)
panels.description: Tables rebuilt from the live store when the server last started.

panels.title: Seats held (last start)
panels.description: Seats held for their reconnect grace period after the last restart.

panels.title: Pots refunded (last start)
panels.description: Open pots with no live table, returned to their contributors through the ledger.

panels.title: Live store latency by operation
panels.description: p95 of each store call from the game server's own timing. Redis on the loopback should stay well under a millisecond.

panels.title: Live store operations
panels.description: Calls per second by operation and result. `stale` is the two-owners guard firing, not an error.

panels.title: Live store errors
panels.description: Failed store calls per second. These never refuse a move: the money is already committed in PostgreSQL.

panels.title: Redis memory and clients
panels.description: Resident memory against the cap, and connected clients (the game server pools a handful).

panels.title: Redis command rate and keyspace
panels.description: Commands per second, and hits versus misses on lookups.
